summary: A personal task manager on localhost: quick-add that understands 'call Sam tomorrow 4pm #home p2', Today and Upcoming views, recurring tasks that behave on the 31st, full-text search, phone reminders through ntfy, and a CLI for capture from any terminal. One SQLite file you can back up.

stack.why: views, forms and a scheduler in one process

stack.choice: chrono-node for dates, rrule for recurrence
stack.why: calendar edge cases look simple until they are wrong on the last day of a month
a phone notification with no app to build

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: The ntfy app on your phone with a private topic
prerequisites.why: Reminders arrive as push notifications through ntfy. No account needed; a long random topic name is the credential.
prerequisites.get: Install ntfy from the App Store or Play Store, subscribe to a topic like tasks-<random 12 chars>, put the topic in .env. Test: curl -d 'hi' ntfy.sh/<topic>.
prerequisites.verify: The test message appears on the phone

prerequisites.name: Your IANA timezone
prerequisites.why: Due dates are plain dates; reminders fire at local times.

prerequisites.name: How 'every 3 days' should count: from the due date or from completion
prerequisites.why: Both are defensible and users assume different ones. Decide the default now; Phase 4 offers the other per task.
prerequisites.get: Default to due-date anchoring for scheduled chores; completion anchoring as a per-task flag for habits.

env.name: PORT
env.where: Bound to 127.0.0.1 or your LAN address.

env.name: TIMEZONE
env.where: IANA zone for reminders and the digest.

env.name: NTFY_TOPIC
env.where: Your private topic from the ntfy app.

env.name: DIGEST_HOUR
env.where: Hour of the morning digest in TIMEZONE.

phases.title: Tasks and projects
phases.goal: The object model and a list that renders; no parsing yet.

steps.do: Create the project and the tables
steps.detail: tasks (id, content, notes, project_id, priority 1-3, due_date YYYY-MM-DD, due_time, rrule, anchor, completed_at, parent_id, position, created_at), projects (id, name, color, archived), completions (id, task_id, completed_at).
commands: mkdir tasks && cd tasks && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.do: Build task CRUD, projects, priorities, notes and completion
steps.detail: Completing writes a completions row. Archiving a project hides its tasks without deleting.

check: A task can be created, edited, completed and uncompleted
Completing writes a completions row
Archiving a project hides its tasks without deleting them

phases.title: Quick add with natural language
phases.goal: One line becomes a task with a date, project and priority, previewed before saving.

steps.do: Install chrono-node and write the parser
steps.detail: Strip #project and pN tokens first, then hand the rest to chrono. Feeding those tokens to the parser produces confident nonsense.

steps.do: Show a live preview of what will be created before commit

check: 'call Sam tomorrow 4pm #home p2' parses correctly
#home does not end up in the title
'next friday' resolves correctly near a month boundary
Text with no date creates a task with no due date, not today

phases.title: Views
phases.goal: Today, Upcoming and per-project, with overdue pinned.

steps.do: Build Today with overdue tasks pinned red at the top and counted
Build Upcoming grouped by day for seven days, and per-project views, each with a deliberate empty state

check: A task due yesterday appears in Today as overdue
A task due in 3 days appears under the right day in Upcoming
Today renders correctly with nothing due

phases.title: Recurrence
phases.goal: rrule strings, the anchor rule you decided, and sane behaviour in February.

steps.do: Install rrule and store recurrence as RRULE strings
Implement the anchor flag and scheduling of the next occurrence on completion
steps.detail: Completing writes a completions row and moves due_date to the next occurrence per the anchor.

check: A monthly task due on the 31st behaves sanely in February
A weekly task completed late schedules from the correct anchor per its flag
Completing never destroys the series
History is visible

phases.title: Search and subtasks
phases.goal: FTS5 search and one level of subtasks.

steps.do: Add an FTS5 table over content and notes, kept in sync by triggers
Add one level of subtasks via parent_id with independent completion

check: Search finds a phrase inside a note
Completing a parent does not complete children
Subtask state is visible on the parent

phases.title: Reminders
phases.goal: Once per task, surviving restarts, plus a morning digest.

steps.do: node-cron every minute: push due tasks to ntfy once
steps.detail: Record notified_at on the task so a restart never re-fires.

steps.do: Send the DIGEST_HOUR digest with the day's list

check: A task due at 14:00 notifies once at 14:00
Restarting at 14:30 does not re-notify
The digest arrives once with the correct list

phases.title: CLI and deploy
phases.goal: Capture from any terminal, backups, a service.

steps.do: Write t add "..." using the same parser
Nightly backup keeping thirty, a systemd unit, the README
steps.detail: README: quick-add syntax with an ambiguous example, the anchor rule and flag, ntfy setup, where the database lives.

check: The CLI creates a task identical to the UI
A restart loses nothing

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the task server is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.
Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: A task manager you could run for your household on your network: reliable reminders, recurrence that is explainable, capture from anywhere.

architecture.swap: Any parser producing the same fields

operations.monitoring: Uptime on /healthz; a missed digest is the alarm.
operations.incident: If the ntfy topic leaks, pick a new one; nothing else is exposed.

releaseGate: Recurrence verified on the 31st, across DST, and late completion
Reminders verified once-only across a restart

notIncluded: Native mobile apps and offline sync; phone access is ntfy plus the web UI on your network.
after: A PWA shell for the phone
Natural-language recurrence ('every other tuesday') mapped to rrule
